title: Optimization help
author: Ok-Cow7945
selftext:
I’ve been working for about two weeks on a space rts game. I know there’s a bunch on the market lately but I wanted to try and combine my favorite features of several different games, kinda like falling frontier but less fancy.  
I’ve been using Codex and a little bit of Gemini. I’m probably 100 prompts in, and I bet half of them have been about optimization. The game currently has two star systems and no ai factions yet, just the player. I want high time compression to speed through slow times. I had “war on the sea” in mind for this. In that games strategic map where nothing is modeled, you can speed up to 1600x, 3200x on some modded maps. My game can’t even handle 64x with the three starting ships sitting idle. I’ve tried and tried to have codex optimize its code. I even asked Gemini to audit what codex was doing and suggest a path forward. They’re both good at laying out a plan that sounds believable but I’m not getting any results. I finally got to a point where it was acceptable (50x compression) and wanted to add in the next feature and as soon as I did, it completely nuked the compression(8x). I’m very new to this so I don’t use pipelines or anything like that. I just want to know how to proceed. Do I need to start over? I already told it once to gut its process and recode, just to end up back at the same result.

comments.author: Drunkendrakon6
comments.body: Your first mistake was using Codex. Switch to Claude. Next go online find videos on game optimization for large open world simulation games have Claude do research or do it yourself.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
Profile to figure out where the time is being spent. 

After you profile, in order,

1. Do less work  
2. Use better data structures   
3. Use faster algorithms   
4. Optimize individual pieces of code
